title: Athlete of the Week: Isaiah Garza - NewsBreak
text:
By Ruben Juarez ,
48 minutes ago
PHARR, Texas (ValleyCentral) — PSJA North sophomore football player Isaiah Garza is having a breakout season for the Raiders.
The sophomore has 13 total touchdowns after having a limited role for the Raiders as a freshman.
“We’ve given him an opportunity, and he’s been able to come through for us,” said Isaiah’s father and PSJA North Offensive Coordinator, Horacio Garza. “It’s a big deal for us. Big deal for me. Big deal for him.”
Horacio proudly watches his son shine from the sideline.
“It’s a lot of fun,” Horacio said. “Been able to be with him for a lot of years. Having a chance to do it at the high school is exciting.”
Isaiah grew up tagging along with his father on football fields.
“Seeing the energy and the brotherhood there is out here on football field was amazing to me,” said the sophomore wide receiver/running back/safety. “I always wanted to be a part of that. So, growing up I new I’d play for my dad and it would be great.”
Last week, Isaiah stepped up for the Raiders in their biggest game of the season to date.
On offense, he opened the scoring with a touchdown reception.
On defense, he intercepted a pass. Garza and the Raiders held Flour Bluff to only three first-half points.
The Raiders beat the Hornets, 19-10, to remain undefeated and clinch the District 15-5A Division I title. The loss was Flour Bluff’s first of the season.
“It felt great to actually beat that team,” Isaiah said. “Losing to them last year hurt us a lot last year as a team. This year, coming in with a different mindset.”
Growing up around his father, Isaiah enjoyed football. Over time, Isaiah realized basketball was his true passion.
“After a hard pee-wee game, I came up to my dad and I told him, ‘Dad, please don’t be mad at me. I love football, but I really want to play basketball. That’s really what I like to do and I enjoy it. ‘”
“Yeah, he broke my heart telling me that,” Horacio said sarcastically. “He’s been able to produce for the basketball team here at North and been able to do both. So, it’s been a big blessing for us.”
As a freshman, Isaiah was named the Rio Grande Valley Basketball Coaches Association Newcomer of the Year.
Isaiah and the Raiders will look to complete an undefeated regular season when they face Rivera on Thursday at Brownsville Veterans High School. Kick-off is at 7:00 p.m.
